paraphrase: The opening names: the auspicious Mother, the great Queen, the empress seated on the lion-throne; she who arose from the fire-altar of consciousness and is intent on accomplishing the gods' purpose.

original.text: śrīmātā śrīmahārājñī śrīmatsiṃhāsaneśvarī / cidagnikuṇḍasambhūtā devakāryasamudyatā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She bears the noose whose nature is attachment and the goad made of anger; the sugarcane bow is the mind and the five arrows are the five subtle elements (tanmātra); her rosy radiance floods the circle of the universe.

original.text: rāgasvarūpapāśāḍhyā krodhākārāṅkuśojjvalā / manorūpekṣukodaṇḍā pañcatanmātrasāyakā / nijāruṇaprabhāpūramajjadbrahmāṇḍamaṇḍalā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She sits on the lap of Śiva-Kāmeśvara, with her beloved under her sway; she dwells on the central peak of Meru as mistress of Śrīnagara, within the palace of wish-gems (Cintāmaṇi), on the seat of the five Brahmas, in the great lotus-forest and the kadamba grove, in the midst of the ocean of nectar.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: The war with Bhaṇḍāsura in names: she rides the Cakrarāja chariot surrounded by hosts of powers; Mantriṇī on the Geyacakra chariot attends her and Daṇḍanāthā (Vārāhī) on the Kiricakra leads the van; Jvālāmālinī raises a wall of fire; Mantriṇī slays Viṣaṅga and Vārāhī slays Viśukra; Gaṇeśa, born of Kāmeśvara's glance, shatters the obstacle-yantra; she destroys Bhaṇḍa and his hosts and revives Kāma burnt by Śiva's eye.
notes: Verse-range from the local e-text (25-30 checked); the closing name on Kāma's revival placed c. v.33 (not checked).
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: Her lotus face is the Vāgbhava section of the mantra, the part from neck to waist is the middle (Kāmarāja) section, and the part below the waist is the Śakti section; she is the root mantra itself, whose body is the three root sections.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She delights in the nectar of kula and guards the kula conventions; she is the kula-woman, dwells within kula, is Kaulinī and the yoginī of kula; she is also beyond kula (akulā), dwells within Samaya and is intent on Samaya conduct.

original.text: kulāṅganā kulāntasthā kaulinī kulayoginī / akulā samayāntasthā samayācāratatparā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She dwells solely in the mūlādhāra, pierces the knot of Brahmā, rises in the maṇipūra, pierces the knot of Viṣṇu, abides in the ājñā-cakra, pierces the knot of Rudra, mounts the thousand-petalled lotus and showers streams of nectar; she shines like a streak of lightning, abides above the six cakras, is the great power, Kuṇḍalinī, fine as a lotus fibre.
notes: The name read 'mahāśaktiḥ' in many editions appears as 'mahāsaktiḥ' in the local stotra e-text; original omitted.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is Bhavānī, reached by contemplation (bhāvanā), the axe for the forest of worldly existence; she loves devotion, is reached by devotion, is won over by devotion, and takes away fear.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is without support, stainless, untainted, pure, eternal, formless, untroubled, without qualities (nirguṇā), without parts (niṣkalā), peaceful, desireless, indestructible, ever-free, changeless, beyond the world-expanse, without support, ever-pure, ever-awake, faultless, without interval — and the series of such negating names continues.

original.text: nirlepā nirmalā nityā nirākārā nirākulā / nirguṇā niṣkalā śāntā niṣkāmā nirupaplavā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts (v. 44)

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is worshipped by the sequence of the great sacrifice, honoured by Mahābhairava, witness of the great Lord's great dance at the end of the great aeon; she is the queen of Mahākāmeśa, Mahātripurasundarī.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is seated on the seat of the five corpses and is of the nature of the five Brahmas; she is made of consciousness, supreme bliss, a mass of knowledge.

original.text: pañcapretāsanāsīnā pañcabrahmasvarūpiṇī / cinmayī paramānandā vijñānaghanarūpiṇī
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is the universal one in waking, Taijasa in dream, Prājña in deep sleep, the fourth (turyā), and she who is devoid of all states.

original.text: viśvarūpā jāgariṇī svapantī taijasātmikā / suptā prājñātmikā turyā sarvāvasthāvivarjitā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She creates in the form of Brahmā, protects in the form of Govinda, withdraws in the form of Rudra, conceals as Īśvarī, grants grace as Sadāśiva, and is devoted to the five acts.

original.text: sṛṣṭikartrī brahmarūpā goptrī govindarūpiṇī / saṃhāriṇī rudrarūpā tirodhānakarīśvarī / sadāśivānugrahadā pañcakṛtyaparāyaṇā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is desirable, and her form is the kāmakalā.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She dwells in Jālandhara and in the Oḍyāṇa seat, and in the circle of the bindu; she is worshipped by the sequence of the secret sacrifice (rahoyāga) and gratified by secret libations.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is immediately gracious, the witness of the universe, and herself without a witness.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is unmanifest and of the form of the manifest and the unmanifest; all-pervading, of many forms, of the form of both knowledge and ignorance (vidyā and avidyā); the moonlight that gladdens the lotus of Mahākāmeśa's eyes.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is immeasurable, self-luminous, beyond the reach of mind and speech; she is consciousness-power and the form of sentience, and also the power of the insentient and of insentient nature; she is the Gāyatrī, the vyāhṛtis and the twilight prayer, served by the twice-born.

original.text: citśaktiś cetanārūpā jaḍaśaktir jaḍātmikā / gāyatrī vyāhṛtiḥ sandhyā dvijavṛndaniṣevitā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts (v. 90)

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is Kurukullā, ruler of kula, dwells in the kula-pit (at the base), and is served by those devoted to the Kaula path.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: Her form is self-awareness (vimarśa); she is the vidyā, and mother of the world beginning with space.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is the knowledge of the self (ātmavidyā), the great knowledge (mahāvidyā), Śrīvidyā, served by Kāma; the sixteen-syllable vidyā, three-peaked (trikūṭā), Kāmakoṭikā.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is the mother of countless crores of universes and of divine form; she grants the state of isolation-liberation (kaivalya); she is Tripurā, worshipped by the three worlds, the three forms (trimūrti), the ruler of the gods.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is free of all limiting adjuncts, devoted to Sadāśiva, sovereign of the tradition (sampradāyeśvarī), and of the form of the circle of gurus (gurumaṇḍala).
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is independent, the ruler of all tantras, of the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti, worshipped by Sanaka and the others, the giver of the knowledge of Śiva.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She delights in the recitation of her names; she is the substratum of the illusory world (mithyā-jagad-adhiṣṭhānā), the giver of liberation and liberation itself.

original.text: nāmapārāyaṇaprītā nandividyā naṭeśvarī / mithyājagadadhiṣṭhānā muktidā muktirūpiṇī
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is of the form of the fifty seats (pīṭha); unfettered, dwelling apart, the mother of heroes, the source of space.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is to be worshipped by those turned inward and is very hard to reach for those turned outward.

original.text: antarmukhasamārādhyā bahirmukhasudurlabhā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is free of disease, without support, delighting in her own self, a flow of nectar; she is skilled in lifting out those sunk in the mire of saṃsāra.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She abides on both the right-hand and the left-hand paths; she is worshipped by followers of the dakṣiṇa and the non-dakṣiṇa ways; she is Kaulinī and the one who alone grants the priceless state of kaivalya.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She is pleased by the worship of suvāsinīs (married women), gratified by the offering into the bindu, the first-born, Tripurāmbikā; worshipped with the ten mudrās, she brings Tripurāśrī under her sway; she is the knowledge-mudrā, reached by knowledge, whose form is knowledge and the known; the yoni-mudrā, lady of the three-part (trikhaṇḍā) mudrā.
speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: She dwells in the Śrīcakra, the king of cakras; she is the glorious Tripurasundarī; the auspicious Śivā, whose form is the oneness of Śiva and Śakti, Lalitāmbikā.

original.text: śrīcakrarājanilayā śrīmattripurasundarī / śrīśivā śivaśaktyaikyarūpiṇī lalitāmbikā
original.edition: stotra text as in the Nirṇayasāgara ed. with Saubhāgyabhāskara; checked against local e-texts

speaker: the Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)

paraphrase: Hayagrīva: commanded by Lalitā, the goddesses of speech composed a supreme hymn of divine secret names; hence it is famed as the 'thousand secret names' (rahasya-nāma-sāhasra).
speaker: Hayagrīva
notes: Numbering of the pūrvabhāga as in the Nirṇayasāgara edition with the Saubhāgyabhāskara (checked).

paraphrase: The concluding section praises the recitation of the thousand names above other rites, lists its fruits, and limits its transmission to devotees of Lalitā.
speaker: Hayagrīva
notes: Summary from memory; verse-level content not checked.

paraphrase: On name 4: 'cit' is Brahman alone; it is the fire-pit because it is opposed to the darkness that is ignorance; from it the Goddess arose.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: On 'Kaulinī' and 'intent on Samaya conduct': kula is Śakti and akula Śiva, and their relation is kaula; worship on a cakra drawn in external space is conventionally called Kaula; imagining the cakra in the inner space of the heart (dahara) and worshipping there is called Samaya; the five tantras of Vasiṣṭha, Śuka, Sanaka, Sanandana and Sanatkumāra are also called Samaya; or Samaya is Śiva, who has fivefold equality with the Goddess (of seat, action, state, name and form), as the commentator on the Subhagodaya (Lalla) set out.
notes: Checked in the local e-text (commentary on verse 88 of the continuous numbering = stotra 37).
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: In the same passage: when the initiate's contemplation of unity is firm and the rite called the great piercing (mahāvedha) has been done, the Goddess, risen from the mūlādhāra, becomes manifest in the maṇipūra; there she is worshipped with offerings, then led to the anāhata, the viśuddhi and the ājñā with further offerings, and united with Sadāśiva in the thousand-petalled lotus.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: On 'devoid of all states': one who has passed beyond the fourth state has passed through the first three and is free of all four; this state beyond the fourth (turyātīta) comes from firmness in the fourth, as the saying 'the state beyond the fourth is gained by holding firmly to the fourth' shows.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: The twelve kinds of Śrīvidyā are those of its twelve worshippers — Manu, Candra, Kubera, Lopāmudrā, Manmatha, Agastya, Agni, Sūrya, Indra, Skanda, Śiva and Krodhabhaṭṭāraka; their derivation is to be seen in the Jñānārṇava.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: On the guru's opening verse: she is Tripurā because her city is threefold — the triangle, circle and square of three lines, and the mantra of three parts (citing the Kālikā Purāṇa).
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: Quoting the Rudrayāmala: after many births of merit one is initiated; then by great fortune one becomes devoted to Śiva or Viṣṇu; then the disposition toward Śakti arises; then by great good fortune the disposition toward Sundarī; then the fourth is reached within; and then, rarest of all, the singing of her names — in that birth the eternal Goddess, pleased by the recitation, grants liberation while living and nothing more remains to be done.

tags.stage_native: the ladder of births culminating in nāma-kīrtana

notes: Quoted by Bhāskararāya in the introduction to the phalaśruti section (checked in local e-text).
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: On the concluding section: recitation is a daily duty yet may by explicit statement also serve desired ends, as with the Agnihotra; the offerings are subsidiaries that share the fruit of the main act; and in worship with the names the principal thing is to contemplate the identity of oneself and the deity.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: The Triśatī gives three hundred names of Lalitā, twenty beginning with each of the fifteen syllables of the Śrīvidyā mantra, so that the hymn as a whole unfolds the mantra.
speaker: Hayagrīva

paraphrase: Hayagrīva calls the Triśatī the most secret of the Goddess's hymns and teaches it only after Agastya's persistent request, restricting it to the devoted and qualified.
speaker: Hayagrīva
notes: From memory of the frame story; not checked.

paraphrase: Śiva, when joined with Śakti, is able to create; if not, the god cannot even stir. How then can one without merit bow to you or praise you, who are worshipped even by Hari, Hara and Viriñci?

original.text: śivaḥ śaktyā yukto yadi bhavati śaktaḥ prabhavituṃ / na ced evaṃ devo na khalu kuśalaḥ spanditum api / atas tvām ārādhyāṃ hariharaviriñcyādibhir api / praṇantuṃ stotuṃ vā katham akṛtapuṇyaḥ prabhavati

speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Brahmā creates the worlds by gathering a tiny speck of dust from your lotus feet; Viṣṇu bears it with his thousand heads; Hara crushes it and smears it on himself as ash.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: For the ignorant you are the city of the sun that dispels inner darkness; for the dull a stream of the honey of consciousness; for the poor a string of wish-gems; for those sunk in the ocean of birth, the tusk of Viṣṇu's boar.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: In the midst of the ocean of nectar, on the jewel-island ringed by wish-trees, in the kadamba grove, in the house of wish-gems, on the Śiva-shaped couch, on Paramaśiva's bed — a blessed few worship you, a wave of consciousness-bliss.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Piercing earth in the mūlādhāra, water in the maṇipūra, fire in the svādhiṣṭhāna, air in the heart, space above it and mind between the brows — the whole kula-path — you sport in secret with your consort in the thousand-petalled lotus.

original.text: mahīṃ mūlādhāre kam api maṇipūre hutavahaṃ / sthitaṃ svādhiṣṭhāne hṛdi marutam ākāśam upari / mano 'pi bhrūmadhye sakalam api bhittvā kulapathaṃ / sahasrāre padme saha rahasi patyā viharasi

notes: The verse assigns water to the maṇipūra and fire to the svādhiṣṭhāna, the reverse of the usual haṭha order.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Sprinkling the world with streams of nectar flowing from between your feet, you return again to your own place, make yourself into a serpent of three and a half coils, and sleep in the hollow of the kula-pit.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: The corners of your dwelling (the Śrīcakra) are formed by four Śrīkaṇṭhas (Śiva triangles) and five Śiva-yuvatīs (Śakti triangles) — nine root natures distinct from Śambhu — making forty-three angles, together with the eight-petalled and sixteen-petalled lotuses, the three circles and the three lines.
notes: Brown's text reads 'trayaś catvāriṃśad' (43); Lakṣmīdhara's commentary counts forty-four.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Whoever meditates on you together with Vaśinī and the other goddesses of speech becomes a maker of great poems, with words sweet as the fragrance of Sarasvatī's lotus-mouth.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Whoever meditates on your kāmakalā — the face as the point, the pair of breasts beneath it and below them the half of Hara — at once stirs women and quickly sways even the three worlds whose breasts are sun and moon.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: The great ones, their minds cleansed of the stain of māyā, behold in the great lotus-forest your digit, slender as a streak of lightning, made of sun, moon and fire, seated above the six lotuses, and hold waves of supreme bliss.

original.text: taḍillekhātanvīṃ tapanaśaśivaiśvānaramayīṃ / niṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaṇṇām apy upari kamalānāṃ tava kalām / mahāpadmāṭavyāṃ mṛditamalamāyena manasā / mahāntaḥ paśyanto dadhati paramāhlādalaharīm

speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Whoever, wishing to pray 'O Bhavānī, you — cast your compassionate glance on me, your servant', has only said 'Bhavāni tvam', to him you at once grant union with you (sāyujya), your feet lit by the crowns of Mukunda, Brahmā and Indra.

original.text: bhavāni tvaṃ dāse mayi vitara dṛṣṭiṃ sakaruṇām / iti stotuṃ vāñchan kathayati bhavāni tvam iti yaḥ / tadaiva tvaṃ tasmai diśasi nijasāyujyapadavīṃ / mukundabrahmendrasphuṭamukuṭanīrājitapadām

notes: 'bhavāni tvam' also means 'may I become you'.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Brahmā creates the world, Hari protects, Rudra destroys; Īśa, concealing all this, conceals even his own body; Sadāśiva favours it all — each relying on your command given by a flicker of your creeper-like brows.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: At the great dissolution Brahmā dies, Hari comes to rest, Yama perishes, Kubera meets his end, even the hosts of Indra close their eyes — yet your husband, O chaste one, sports on.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Let my idle talk be japa, every movement of my hands a mudrā, my walking circumambulation, my eating and the rest oblation, my lying down prostration — whatever I do, with the attitude of self-offering, let it be a form of your worship.

original.text: japo jalpaḥ śilpaṃ sakalam api mudrāviracanā / gatiḥ prādakṣiṇyakramaṇam aśanādy āhutividhiḥ / praṇāmaḥ saṃveśaḥ sukham akhilam ātmārpaṇadṛśā / saparyāparyāyas tava bhavatu yan me vilasitam

speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: The verse encodes the fifteen letters of the Goddess's mantra, naming each by a deity or element, in three groups each closed by the syllable called hṛllekhā; these letters become the members of her name. (Summary only; the syllables are not reproduced.)
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Some eternal ones, relishing boundless great enjoyment, place three seed-syllables at the head of your mantra and do japa with rosaries of wish-gems, offering streams of fragrant ghee into the fire of Śiva. (Summary; syllables not reproduced.)
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: You are Śambhu's body, with sun and moon for breasts; your self I consider to be the stainless Bhava; hence the relation of principal and subsidiary is common to you both, who are intent on the same supreme bliss.
notes: Lakṣmīdhara reads 'navātmānam' for Brown's 'bhavātmānam' and takes the verse as the pūrva-Kaula view.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: You are mind, you are space, you are air and the charioteer of air (fire), you are water, you are earth; when you have transformed yourself there is nothing beyond. To transform your own self into the form of the universe you bear, as Śiva's young wife, the form of consciousness-bliss.

original.text: manas tvaṃ vyoma tvaṃ marud asi marutsārathir asi / tvam āpas tvaṃ bhūmis tvayi pariṇatāyāṃ na hi param / tvam eva svātmānaṃ pariṇamayituṃ viśvavapuṣā / cidānandākāraṃ śivayuvati bhāvena bibhṛṣe

speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: The poet worships the Śiva-Śakti pair in each cakra: in the ājñā the supreme Śambhu joined with supreme consciousness; in the viśuddhi the crystal-clear Śiva who begets space, with the Goddess; in the heart the pair of swans who, like drawing milk from water, take the good from faults; in the svādhiṣṭhāna the fire of dissolution and the great Samayā; in the maṇipūra the dark cloud with its lightning that rains on the scorched worlds.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: In your mūlādhāra I worship Navātman, dancing the great tāṇḍava full of the nine sentiments, together with Samayā intent on the gentle dance (lāsya); from these two, acting with compassion for the twofold purpose of creation, this world was born, having a father and a mother.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: You are the inner palace of the destroyer of the Cities; the worship of your feet is not easy for those of restless senses; so Indra and the gods won incomparable powers only by waiting at your gate with Aṇimā and the other powers.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: For one who always contemplates you, attended on all sides by Aṇimā and the other powers — rays born of your own body — as 'I am you', what wonder that the fire of the great dissolution waves lights before him, who counts the wealth of the three-eyed one as straw?
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Knowers of the āgamas call you Speech, the wife of Brahmā; Padmā, the wife of Hari; the mountain's daughter, Hara's companion; but you are a certain fourth, hard to reach, of boundless greatness — O Mahāmāyā, queen of the supreme Brahman, you make the universe whirl.

original.text: girām āhur devīṃ druhiṇagṛhiṇīm āgamavido / hareḥ patnīṃ padmāṃ harasahacarīm adritanayām / turīyā kāpi tvaṃ duradhigamaniḥsīmamahimā / mahāmāye viśvaṃ bhramayasi parabrahmamahiṣi

speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Your worshipper sports with Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī, rivalling Brahmā and Hari, and with a beautiful body loosens Rati's fidelity; living long, the entanglement of the bound soul's bonds destroyed, he tastes the rasa called the supreme Brahman.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Like waving the flames of a lamp before the sun, offering water to the moon from drops of moonstone, or satisfying the ocean with its own waters — so is this hymn to you, Mother of speech, made of your own words.

original.text: pradīpajvālābhir divasakaranīrājanavidhiḥ / sudhāsūteś candropalajalalavair arghyaghaṭanā / svakīyair ambhobhiḥ salilanidhisauhityakaraṇaṃ / tvadīyābhir vāgbhis tava janani vācāṃ stutir iyam

speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)

paraphrase: Worship of the cakra is of two kinds: in the outer space — drawing it on a seat, birch-bark, cloth or a plate of gold or silver — which the elders call Kaula worship; and in the space of the heart (dahara), which the Samayins call Samaya worship. The bindu between the four lower Śiva-yonis and the five upper Śakti-yonis is the ocean of nectar of the verse.
speaker: Lakṣmīdhara

paraphrase: The moon-disc in the head, known to all the yoga texts, is for the Samayins the Śrīcakra itself, since the moon has sixteen digits and the digits of Śrīvidyā wax and wane over the sixteen lunar days; even the outer moon is the Śrīcakra, a great secret. The Goddess drenches the practitioner's whole body with the nectar of her feet in the crown, then enters the base as a serpent and sleeps.
speaker: Lakṣmīdhara

paraphrase: The twenty-five principles are accepted by all because the Veda teaches them; the thirty-six-principle scheme is to be read in their light; beyond all principles is the conjoined pair of Śiva and Śakti, the twenty-sixth, from which the world arises; the one who knows it attains, by degrees of worship, the fivefold liberation of equal power, same world, nearness, same form and union (sārṣṭi, sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya, sāyujya).
speaker: Lakṣmīdhara

paraphrase: The verse may also state the uttara-Kaula doctrine: in it there is no Śiva-principle apart from the Śakti-principle, so Śiva is included in Śakti and she alone is to be worshipped — a view Lakṣmīdhara promises to examine at verses 35 and 41.
speaker: Lakṣmīdhara

paraphrase: Introducing the Samaya doctrine of verses 36-41, the commentator first sets out the Kaula doctrine, which is twofold: the pūrva-Kaula (verse 34) and the uttara-Kaula (verse 35).
speaker: Lakṣmīdhara

paraphrase: Samayā is she who attains fivefold equality with Śambhu, and Śambhu too attains fivefold equality with the Goddess, so both are of equal primacy: equality of seat (both in the ādhāra), of action (both generate the world), of state (lāsya and tāṇḍava are one as dance), of form (both are red) and of name. For the Samayins the worship is of Samayā and Samaya in the thousand-petalled lotus; outer worship and the worship of a young woman's triangle are wholly rejected.
speaker: Lakṣmīdhara

paraphrase: Introducing the next verse: by the power of contemplating the fourfold unity, the Samayins see the Goddess's form shining in the maṇipūra.
speaker: Lakṣmīdhara

paraphrase: Even the supreme, when without Śakti, cannot do anything; O great Goddess, he becomes able only when joined with Śakti.

original.text: paro 'pi śaktirahitaḥ śaktaḥ kartuṃ na kiñcana / śaktaḥ syāt parameśāni śaktyā yukto bhaved yadi
original.edition: as quoted by Lakṣmīdhara on SL 11 (Mysore ed.)

notes: Known here only through Lakṣmīdhara's quotation.

paraphrase: Whatever the child's faults in worship and duty, the Mother forgives: a bad son may be born, but never a bad mother.

original.text: kuputro jāyeta kvacid api kumātā na bhavati

speaker: the devotee

paraphrase: Brahmā names the nine Durgās: first Śailaputrī, second Brahmacāriṇī, third Candraghaṇṭā, fourth Kūṣmāṇḍā, fifth Skandamātā, sixth Kātyāyanī, seventh Kālarātri, eighth Mahāgaurī, ninth Siddhidātrī.
speaker: Brahmā

paraphrase: Each verse praises the Goddess by one of her deeds and asks: give beauty, give victory, give glory, destroy enemies.

original.text: rūpaṃ dehi jayaṃ dehi yaśo dehi dviṣo jahi

paraphrase: Medhas to the king: the supreme Mahālakṣmī, possessing the three qualities, the first of all, pervades the manifest and unmanifest; from her tamas she brought forth Mahākālī and from her sattva Mahāsarasvatī; from the three arose three divine pairs, and Mahālakṣmī gave each god his consort, so that the world is created, preserved and destroyed.
speaker: Medhas
notes: From memory; the assignment of the couples is not recorded here and the verse range is approximate.

paraphrase: The Goddess asks Bhairava: in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra there are many matters whose meaning is not known; explain them all.
speaker: the Goddess

paraphrase: Bhairava: hear, O Goddess, the great secret, the supreme Yoginīhṛdaya; out of love for you I tell it today; it must be guarded with special care.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: The code (saṅketa) of the goddess Tripurā is threefold: the code of the cakra, the code of the mantra and the code of worship.

original.text: cakrasaṅketako mantrapūjāsaṅketakau tathā / trividhas tripurādevyāḥ saṅketaḥ parameśvari

speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: When the supreme Śakti, of her own will taking the form of the universe, beholds her own vibrancy (sphurattā), then the cakra comes into being.

original.text: yadā sā paramā śaktiḥ svecchayā viśvarūpiṇī / sphurattām ātmanaḥ paśyet tadā cakrasya sambhavaḥ

speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: This cakra is ninefold and has nine distinct mantras.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: The four powers, fused in pairs, became the four seats Kāmarūpa, Pūrṇagiri, Jālandhara and Oḍḍiyāna; the seats stand in order in the bulb (kanda), in pada, in rūpa and beyond form (rūpātīta).
notes: 1.41 as read with the Dīpikā, which glosses the four syllables as the four pīṭhas; 1.42 root checked.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: Thus the code of the great cakra of Tripurā has been told, O supreme Goddess, which brings about liberation while living.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: The mantra-code is sixfold: the literal meaning (bhāvārtha), the traditional meaning (sampradāyārtha), the hidden meaning (nigarbhārtha), the Kaula meaning (kaulikārtha), the all-secret meaning (sarvarahasyārtha) and the meaning of the great principle (mahātattvārtha); the literal meaning is simply the sense of the syllables.

original.text: bhāvārthaḥ sampradāyārtho nigarbhārthaś ca kaulikaḥ / tathā sarvarahasyārtho mahātattvārtha eva ca

speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: The hidden meaning (nigarbha) has as its domain Śiva, the guru and the self.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: The Kaula meaning is the oneness of the cakra and the deity, and of the vidyā, the guru and the self.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: The meaning of the great principle: in the partless, supreme, subtle, unmarkable principle, free of all states, beyond space, whose body is light and bliss, transcending and pervading the universe — (the self is to be dissolved there).
notes: Only the opening of the passage checked; the closing clause is summarized from the Dīpikā's gloss.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: Those who lack the succession of teachers and are proud of mere knowledge — through their breach of the samaya the rays (marīci) turn against them.

original.text: pāramparyavihīnā ye jñānamātreṇa garvitāḥ / teṣāṃ samayalopena vikurvanti marīcayaḥ

speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: Thus this supreme knowledge, the domain of the letters of the vidyā and the āgamas, secret and sixfold, hard to penetrate, has been explained; by awakening to it one at once becomes lord of the circle of heroes.
notes: Wording as in the Setubandha text (paṭala 7 end).
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: Now I shall tell the code of worship, by merely awakening to which one rejoices, liberated while living.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: Your worship, ever arisen, is of three kinds: the supreme (parā), the non-supreme (aparā) and the supreme-non-supreme (parāparā). The first abides in non-duality and ranges over every outflow of the senses; the second, the worship of the cakra, is always performed by me.
speaker: Bhairava (Śiva)

paraphrase: Saṅketa means a tryst: as lovers who have agreed on a meeting place meet there, so Śiva and Śakti meet in the cakra, the mantra and the worship. Tripurā is she who exists before (purā) the three — abodes, principles, seats, liṅgas, letters — the supreme, whose nature is the fusion (sāmarasya) of light (prakāśa) and self-awareness (vimarśa).
speaker: Amṛtānanda

paraphrase: Liberation while living is release from bondage by the eight fetters beginning with disgust; the one who has grasped the cakra-code through the guru forcibly destroys all fetters and sets going the contemplation 'I am Śiva'.
speaker: Amṛtānanda

paraphrase: Supreme worship is not the daily offering of outer flowers and substances; it is abiding in one's own great non-dual abode (quoting the Saṅketapaddhati). Wherever the mind goes, outside or inside, there is the supreme state (quoting the Vijñānabhairava). The parāparā worship is meditative, dissolving the outer into the inner non-dual abode of consciousness.
speaker: Amṛtānanda

paraphrase: The aparā worship — worship of the enclosure-deities of the Śrīcakra from the square to the bindu — is done daily even by the all-knowing, because it produces the conviction of non-difference; all knowers should perform it, otherwise non-duality would be a mere denial of what was never in question.
speaker: Amṛtānanda

paraphrase: The Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava and the Yoginīhṛdaya are the prior and latter 'four-hundreds' of one Vāmakeśvara tantra, and their unity of purport is beyond dispute: the nyāsas taught in the first are presupposed in the second, and what the second extracts is not given in the first. For those firm in inner worship the Yoginīhṛdaya's inner worship suffices even though few outer subsidiaries are stated.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: 'Secret' (guhya) means what lies in the cave: the identity of the individual self and the supreme self, as the Upaniṣads say; because worship has that as its fruit, it too is secret, and it is twofold, outer and inner.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: The steady flow of the mind toward this meaning is gained only by the grace of the guru's feet, not by knowledge of scripture alone.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: Tripurā goes to the supreme Person, markless, without qualities, devoid of the form of kula; then, free in her own form, taking the Lord of the world to herself and pleased by that path, she, alone, sports by herself — unmanifest Tripurā come to manifestation.
speaker: Bhairava
notes: Known here through the Yoginīhṛdayadīpikā's quotation (on YH 2.69-72, citing NṢA 4.12-16); only the latter part was seen, so the paraphrase is partial.

paraphrase: The tantra teaches how the Śrīcakra is drawn — the central point, the triangles, the eight- and sixteen-petalled lotuses and the square — and how it is worshipped enclosure by enclosure with its deities, placements (nyāsa) and ten mudrās.
speaker: Bhairava
notes: Chapter-level summary; exact paṭala not recorded.

paraphrase: Around Tripurasundarī, the sixteenth, are the fifteen Nityās, each with her mantra, form and rite, worshipped in the triangle of the cakra.
speaker: Bhairava
notes: Chapter-level summary.

paraphrase: The Goddess: the nine tantras of the sixteen Nityās depend on one another and bewilder the mind; tell me a tantra of theirs that needs no other. Śiva: hear the Kādimata tantra, complete without dependence on others, to be guarded with every effort, as tantric teaching enjoins.
speaker: Śiva and the Goddess

paraphrase: Asked why it is named Kādimata, Śiva says that the two Śaktis Kādi and Kālī had earlier been taught by him in tantras named after their doctrines, and hence the name.
speaker: Śiva
notes: The sense of the verse is uncertain; checked only in part.

paraphrase: The table of contents ends: the thirty-third paṭala gives yantras for different fruits, the thirty-fourth the names, the thirty-fifth the inner meaning (vāsanā), the thirty-sixth the teaching on one's own self; each chapter has about a hundred verses — such is the compass of the tantra.
speaker: Śiva

original.text: ṣaṭtriṃśe svātmakathanam adhyāyās tattvavigrahāḥ / pratyadhyāyaṃ śataślokāḥ syād evaṃ tantrasaṅgrahaḥ

paraphrase: The sixteen Nityās are the digits of the moon and the lunar days; time itself — the days and their divisions down to the breath — is their form, and the practitioner worships the Nityā presiding over each day.
notes: Summary from memory of the Tantrarāja's time-correlations; paṭala references not recorded.

paraphrase: May Maheśa protect us, whose body is pure light, within whom self-awareness lies merged, who delights in the play of the arising, abiding and dissolving of all worlds. Victorious is the primal Śakti, whose form is her own eternal incomparable bliss, the seed of all that moves and does not move, the stainless mirror in which Śiva's form is reflected. The supreme Śakti is the sprout of the seed that is the manifest union of Śiva and Śakti.

original.text: sakalabhuvanodayasthitilayamayalīlāvinodanodyuktaḥ / antarlīnavimarśaḥ pātu maheśaḥ prakāśamātratanuḥ

speaker: Puṇyānanda

paraphrase: When the rays of the sun that is Paraśiva are reflected in the clear mirror of self-awareness, the great point (mahābindu) enters the wall of consciousness; the 'I' made of consciousness, the fused form of the letters 'a' and 'ha', the lump of Śiva and Śakti in union, which has swallowed the circle of the worlds, is victorious.
speaker: Puṇyānanda

paraphrase: The pair of points, white and red, is Śiva and Śakti separated, contracting and expanding, entering one another, the cause of the creation of word and meaning; the point that is the 'I' is the sun, the fused form of this pair; kāma (desire) because it is lovely, and kalā — the two points that are fire and moon. This is the kāmakalā-vidyā, whose nature is the sequence of the Goddess's cakra; whoever knows it is liberated, becoming Mahātripurasundarī.
speaker: Puṇyānanda

paraphrase: Victorious is that great light: when it is seen, nothing else is seen; and yet the Veda says that when it is known all is known — how can that be?

original.text: sa jayati mahān prakāśo yasmin dṛṣṭe na dṛśyate kim api / katham iva tasmiñ jñāte sarvaṃ vijñātam ucyate vede

speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: In pronouncing the mantra's final sounds the voice passes through subtle phases — bindu, ardhacandra, rodhinī, nāda, nādānta, śakti, vyāpikā, samanā and unmanā — each lasting half as long as the one before, from 128 units down to one for samanā; unmanā has no time at all.
notes: From the auto-commentary Prakāśa in part one (a mātrā = 256 units); verse number not recorded.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: Uttering a word without knowing its meaning bears no fruit, as oblation thrown on ash without fire does not blaze; those who recite many words without knowing their sense are like an ass carrying sandalwood; those who want the aims of life must learn the meanings — for those who disregard meaning there is no gain but harm.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: The meanings of the full Gāyatrī (the Pañcadaśī) are fifteen, equal to its syllables: the first (the Gāyatrī meaning), then the literal, traditional, hidden (the fourth), Kaula, secret and great-principle meanings, the meaning of the name, of the sound-form, of part of the name, of the Śaktas, of fusion (sāmarasya), the collective, the qualified, and the meaning of the great saying.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: The blessed Paramaśiva, having in play composed the eighteen sciences beginning with the Veda and all the philosophical schools, taking on the corresponding states, was questioned by the Goddess Bhairavī, made of consciousness and not different from himself, and through his five faces set forth the five transmissions (āmnāya), the essence of the highest truth.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: The universe is the thirty-six principles.

original.text: ṣaṭtriṃśattattvāni viśvam

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Śiva clothed in body and coverings is the individual soul (jīva); Śiva free of coverings is Paraśiva.

original.text: śarīrakañcukitaḥ śivo jīvo niṣkañcukaḥ paraśivaḥ

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Awareness of oneself (svavimarśa) is the goal of human life.

original.text: svavimarśaḥ puruṣārthaḥ

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Words made of letters are eternal; mantras have inconceivable power.

original.text: varṇātmakā nityāḥ śabdāḥ // mantrāṇām acintyaśaktitā

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: All success comes through the tradition (sampradāya) and faith (viśvāsa); validity consists above all in faith.

original.text: saṃpradāyaviśvāsābhyāṃ sarvasiddhiḥ // viśvāsabhūyiṣṭhaṃ prāmāṇyam

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Knowledge of the inner self comes from realizing the oneness of guru, mantra, deity, self, mind and breath.

original.text: gurumantradevatātmamanaḥpavanānām aikyaniṣphālanād antarātmavittiḥ

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Bliss is the form of Brahman and it resides in the body; the five 'M's manifest it; worship with them is to be done in secret, and making it public leads to hell. (Summary only.)
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: From firmness of contemplation (bhāvanā) comes the power of command (ājñā-siddhi).

original.text: bhāvanādārḍhyād ājñāsiddhiḥ

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: The conduct of the initiate: no censure of any philosophical school; disregard of no one; the secret told only to a worthy disciple; constant holding of the vidyā; constant immersion in Śiva-hood; avoidance of desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, envy, unsanctioned violence, theft and what the world detests; worship of one guru without doubt; non-possessiveness everywhere; action done without regard to fruit; omission of non-obligatory rites; continuation of the daily worship even when the five 'M's are unavailable; fearlessness everywhere.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: All that is knowable is the oblation, the senses are the ladles, the powers are the flames, one's own self is Śiva, the fire, and oneself is the offerer; the fruit is awareness of consciousness free of objects; there is nothing higher than gaining the self.

original.text: sarvaṃ vedyaṃ havyam indriyāṇi srucaḥ śaktayo jvālāḥ svātmā śivaḥ pāvakaḥ svayam eva hotā // nirviṣayacidvimṛṣṭiḥ phalam // ātmalābhān na paraṃ vidyate

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: The Veda and the other sciences are public, like courtesans; this vidyā is hidden in all the schools.

original.text: veśyā iva prakaṭā vedādividyāḥ / sarveṣu darśaneṣu gupteyaṃ vidyā

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: The wise should by all means take initiation. Initiations are three: śāktī, by the entry of power; śāmbhavī, by the placing of the (guru's) foot; māntrī, by the imparting of mantra; all should be given — or, some say, any one.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: In initiation the guru contemplates on the disciple's head the red and white feet, adorning his whole body washed in their nectar, then meditates on a wave of light blazing like fire from the base to the aperture of Brahmā and burns away the disciple's sins and bonds with its rays.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: The guru whispers the Bālā mantra into the disciple's right ear and then the chosen mantra; gives him a name of two to four syllables ending in '-ānandanātha'; and before the Bālā teaching gives him his own pādukā.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Having taught the rules of conduct and touched the disciple's heart-consciousness, the guru embraces him, smells his head and makes him his own self; the disciple, contemplating fullness, fulfilled, honours the guru with wealth as he can and becomes one who knows what is to be known, entitled to all mantras.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Rising in the hour before dawn, the initiate contemplates the guru's feet in the thousand-petalled lotus of the crown, his whole body flooded by the nectar flowing from them; then meditates on Gaṇapati in the heart, and after the morning duties offers libations.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: In the great cakra the worshipper contemplates and honours, with forty-four mantras, the Goddess's world: the ocean of nectar, the jewel island, gardens of wish-trees, the jewelled ramparts, halls and pools of nectar, bliss and self-awareness, the great lotus forest, the palace of wish-gems whose four doors are the four transmissions, and the couch whose legs are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara and whose plank is Sadāśiva.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: The Goddess is served with sixty-four royal services (catuḥṣaṣṭy-upacāra): ornaments removed, anointing with oil, bath, garments, unguents, flowers, jewels from crown to foot, the noose, goad, sugarcane bow and flower arrows, mounting the great cakra with the enclosure deities dressed like her, sitting on Kāmeśvara's lap, drink, betel, lights, parasol, fans, mirror and the rest.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: One steadfast in kula who knows all this and performs it duly has accomplished everything; at the body's fall it makes no difference whether it is in an outcaste's house or in Kāśī — he is liberated while living.

original.text: itthaṃ viditvā vidhivad anuṣṭhitavataḥ kulaniṣṭhasya sarvataḥ kṛtakṛtyatā śarīratyāge śvapacagṛhakāśyor nāntaraṃ jīvanmuktaḥ

speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Whoever studies this ten-section great Upaniṣad, the whole treasure of the great Traipura doctrine, becomes the performer of all sacrifices; whatever rite he studies, by it his sacrifice is accomplished.
notes: Arthavāda-style praise of study.
speaker: Paraśurāma (by tradition)

paraphrase: Three cities, three paths, the all-ruling one: here the imperishable syllables are set; presiding over them is the unaging, ancient one, the greatest glory of the gods.
They held nine yonis, nine cakras, nine yogas and nine yoginīs; the kindly lords of the nine cakras, nine mudrās, nine blessed ones of the earth.
The great lunar day, the fifteen Nityās, together with the sixteenth, bears the centre of the city.
notes: Obscure verse; paraphrase of the second half only.

paraphrase: Bhaga is Śakti and the blessed Kāma is the Lord; both here are givers of good fortune; they are equal in primacy, equal in being, equal in vigour; their Śakti is unaging, the womb of the universe.

The guru is the Śakti that is the cause of all; so the body with its nine openings is the Śrīcakra of nine cakras; Vārāhī is the father, Kurukullā the mother; the aims of life are the oceans; the body is the island of nine jewels; the fourteen channels are the deities of the fourteen triangles; the ten vital airs are the outer ten, the ten fires the inner ten; cold, heat, pleasure, pain, desire and the three qualities are Vaśinī and the other goddesses of speech; the five subtle elements are the five flower-arrows, mind the sugarcane bow, attachment the noose, aversion the goad; the unmanifest, mahat and ahaṃkāra are Kāmeśvarī, Vajreśvarī and Bhagamālinī in the inner triangle; the fifteen Nityās are the lunar days, the unfolding of time.
The knower is the offerer (hotṛ), knowledge is the fire, the known is the oblation; contemplating the non-difference of knower, knowing and known is the worship of the Śrīcakra.

original.text: jñātā hotā jñānam agnir jñeyaṃ haviḥ / jñātṛjñānajñeyānām abhedabhāvanaṃ śrīcakrapūjanam

paraphrase: The offerings are inward: the readiness of the inner and outer senses is the invocation; their grasping one object the seat; the union of the three states the betel; the movement from the base to the crown and back the circumambulation; the fourth state the prostration; the immersion of the body-identified knower the bali-offering; the dissolving of 'is', 'is not', 'to be done' and 'not to be done' in the eternal self the fire-offering; immersion in her sandals the complete meditation.

One who is thus absorbed in this contemplation for three muhūrtas becomes liberated while living; identity with the deity is accomplished; what he intends comes about without effort; he is called a Śiva-yogin. The bhāvanā has been taught according to the Kādi and Hādi doctrines.

Now the inquiry into dharma. Knowledge and understanding; knowledge is the sole cause of liberation; liberation is the accomplishment of being the self of all; the five objects are the world-expanse; beings are of the nature of knowers; yoga is liberation.

original.text: athāto dharmajijñāsā / jñānaṃ buddhiś ca / jñānaṃ mokṣaikakāraṇam / mokṣaḥ sarvātmatāsiddhiḥ

paraphrase: The very ignorance that is the cause of non-dharma is knowledge; the world is the Lord; the impermanent is permanent; ignorance is knowledge; non-dharma itself is dharma; this is liberation.
notes: Bhāskararāya glosses each as 'nothing is other than Śakti' (e.g. the impermanent jar is the eternal Śakti).

paraphrase: The five bonds are forms of knowledge; from the body comes birth; in that very body is liberation.
notes: Bhāskararāya: liberation happens here, without the delay of departing through the channels on the path of the gods (citing 'his breaths do not depart').

paraphrase: One should not tell one's own secret; one should tell it to a disciple. Inwardly a Śākta, outwardly a Śaiva, among people a Vaiṣṇava: this is the conduct. Liberation comes from knowledge of the self. One should not censure the (other) worlds/views.

original.text: antaḥ śāktaḥ bahiḥ śaivaḥ loke vaiṣṇavaḥ / ayam evācāraḥ / ātmajñānān mokṣaḥ / lokān na nindyāt

paraphrase: On 'one should not censure': the many schools, beginningless in their flow, are all valid for their respective qualified followers; censuring them breeds doubt in those followers, who then lose faith in their own school while not qualified for the Kaula — falling from both; hence Kṛṣṇa's 'one should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant' and Paraśurāma's 'no censure of any school'.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: On 'inwardly a Śākta': the worship of Śakti is to be known by the inner organ alone; the outer Śākta marks are to be covered by Śaiva marks such as ash, since Śiva is not different from Śakti; in assemblies one shows Viṣṇu-worship, Viṣṇu being a manifest form of Tripurasundarī — which is why the Sahasranāma ranks Viṣṇu, Śiva and Śakti devotion as ever more secret.
speaker: Bhāskararāya

paraphrase: Having taken Śambhu's left half, your mind still unsatisfied, you seem to have taken his other half too; for your whole form is red, three-eyed, bowed by the breasts and crowned with the crescent moon.
notes: Lakṣmīdhara reads the verse alternatively as stating the uttara-Kaula doctrine.
speaker: the poet (Śaṅkara, by tradition)
